To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the emergence of a superordinate allied health professional identity and a corporate boardroom management style are key factors in facilitating entrepreneurial approaches to the management of allied health professionals in the public sector.

entrepreneurial approaches within public sector health organisations are more likely to be stimulated when: (1) there is an entrepreneurial leadership culture; (2) there is an external orientation that is opportunity oriented; (3) the corporate boardroom model is in place; (4) the corporate board has an entrepreneurial orientation; and (5) the organisation has a strong superordinate identity.

corporate entrepreneurship is stimulated by the following factors: a strong superordinate identity, the emergence of a single united allied health stakeholder, the development of a boardroom model of managing and a corporate culture that is entrepreneurial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of two different modes of organising allied health professions within the public sector.
the development of two contrasting modes of organising that are based on different cultures and different external orientations.
the development and evolution of two distinct models that have emerged within the allied health sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factors that were observed to stimulate corporate entrepreneurship in the private sector are also the same factors that stimulate corporate entrepreneur ship within the public sector.
there are no significant differences between the factors that stimulated corporate entrepreneurship in Sadlers' study and the factors that stimulated it in the case study.

corporate entrepreneurship was stimulated by the presence of the following factors: (i) a superordinate identity, (ii) a corporate boardroom management model, (iii) a strong entrepreneurial culture, (iv) a corporate strategy that focused on asset creation and growth, and (v) an external orientation of opportunity seeking and risk taking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the case study provided evidence that the factors that stimulate entrepreneurship in the private sector were also present in the public sector.

our study has shown that corporate entrepreneurship can exist within the public sector and that it is possible to identify the factors that stimulate this entrepreneurial activity in a public health service organisation.
the factors that Sadler (2000) found to be significant in stimulating corporate entrepreneurship in the public sector were also significant in stimulating corporate entrepreneur ship in our study.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of corporate entrepreneurship in the public sector is possible, and the presence of corporate entrepreneur ship is more likely to occur when the organisation is structured in a way that allows it to focus on asset growth rather than asset protection, and where its external orientation is opportunity oriented rather than threat oriented.
corporate entrepreneurship can be stimulated in the public sector.
it was possible to identify the key elements that are necessary for corporate entrepreneurship to occur in the public sector.
